brief: Today's posts centered on AI agents coordinating with each other, including the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident and new agent tools. Beyond that, Guillermo Rauch noted that AI Gateway token demand on Vercel has grown about 40% month over month.

themes.label: Agent message boards
themes.summary: Builders described message boards as a coordination layer for agents, citing Replit Missions and Vercel's headless Slack-style board primitive.

themes.label: Google Project Genie and Gemini
themes.summary: Google Labs and Josh Woodward announced Project Genie on Genie 4 and Gemini 4 Neon, with new agents and world-building features.

themes.label: Agents that run continuously
themes.summary: Aaron Levie and Google Labs described agents moving from answering questions to orchestrating long-running work, with Stitch Loop opening a waitlist.

builders.name: Amjad Masad
builders.summary: Pointed to the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident and said Replit Missions lets you watch agents coordinate and talk to each other.

builders.name: AI & I by Every
builders.summary: Shared a podcast episode with Notion founder Ivan Zhao on how AI changes no-code software building.

builders.name: Guillermo Rauch
builders.summary: Introduced Vercel's agent message board as headless Slack for agents, and said AI Gateway token demand has grown about 40% month over month.

builders.name: Josh Woodward
builders.summary: Introduced Gemini 4 Neon as faster and cheaper, and announced a new Project Genie experience for Google AI Ultra subscribers.

builders.name: Google Labs
builders.summary: Launched Stitch Loop, an always-on product agent with a waitlist, and Project Genie on Genie 4 with live prompting and a gallery.

builders.name: Aaron Levie
builders.summary: Argued that agents are moving toward setting goals and designing and improving solutions on their own over long-running work.

builders.name: Nikunj Kothari
builders.summary: Gave founders fundraising advice to lead with what they believe will be true if the company succeeds, and joked about VC liquidity.

builders.name: Thibault Sottiaux
builders.summary: Said GPT-6.2 Astra performs well on the hardest tasks, shared chip optimization results, and asked how 6.2 Sol is treating people.

builders.name: Sam Altman
builders.summary: Praised Greg Brockman in a DealBook appearance, saying OpenAI would not exist without him.

builders.name: Thariq
builders.summary: Said making your own software is hard because it is hard to know what you want, and that good software reflects strong opinions.

builders.name: Aditya Agarwal
builders.summary: Argued early-stage VCs can invest in AI by taking more risk and working on frontier problems, and said stablecoins may aid US soft power.

builders.name: Swyx
builders.summary: Posted mostly short personal and light posts today, including a note that the company is FCF profitable.

builders.name: Peter Yang
builders.summary: Raised questions about why Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia and the board's rapid move on.

builders.name: Dan Shipper
builders.summary: Posted mostly personal and minor updates, including an invitation to a stream with almost 4k people.

builders.name: Zara Zhang
builders.summary: Advised building a system that is a little viral every week rather than massively viral once, and shared a post about Stripe Press books.

builders.name: Nan Yu
builders.summary: Posted a short personal remark with no substantive content.
